_note: THE CHARACTER SLOT. scripts/knight.gd reads this and nothing else about who the occupant is. `clips` maps the ROLES the scene drives to whatever the GLB calls them; `clips_armed` is the SECOND set, used whenever every piece in `armed_when_pieces` is equipped. `forward_axis` is the direction the MODEL faces in its own space -- MEASURED from the walk clip's stance foot. Speeds come from each clip's OWN stride so the feet do not slide, and they are quoted at `speed_measured_at_scale`: knight.gd rescales them to whatever figure scale is live, because a smaller man takes smaller steps.
_speed_scale_note: walk_px_s/run_px_s were derived at figure scale 1.25178 and were being driven unchanged at the 1.10 default, so his legs were 13.8% slow for the ground. Measured: the walk clip's stance-foot floor is 6.8 mm/frame median at 1.25178 and 11.4 mm at 1.10 (24 of 39 pairs under 10 mm against 13 of 39). Roughly 40% of what was recorded as the walk clip's own floor was this. knight.gd now scales both speeds by _figure_scale / speed_measured_at_scale.
_armed_speed_note: MEASURED, tools/probe_stride_armed.gd (in-place clips) and tools/probe_root.gd (travelling ones). walk_armed is IN PLACE: 42 frames / 1.7500 s for a 2.0625 m world stride = 118.6 px/s by the all-frames stance median and 115.4 by the contact-filtered one (6 pairs) -- 2.8% apart, which is the agreement that makes either usable. The unarmed 201.7 would slide his feet 70%. run_armed and strafe_L_armed carry ROOT MOTION and state their own speeds once de-rooted (4.337 m/s and 0.931 m/s), so no number for them is stored here: knight.gd reads the speed off the track it removed, which cannot go stale.
_walk_armed_angle_finding: walk_armed's travel is +9.6 deg off the model's +Z, contact-filtered (walk's is +0.0). An EARLIER figure of 24.3 deg in this file was my own instrument: the all-frames median takes the lower foot on every frame, and on a clip that is airborne or swinging for most of them that is a SWINGING foot. Not compensated in the scene -- 9.6 deg is small and a weight-dependent yaw offset would put a rotation into the walk-run transitions.

_measured.walk: stride 1.6680 m per 1.0417 s cycle -> 2.004 m/s at figure scale -> 201.7 canvas px/s (0.82x the Keeper's 247)
_measured.run: stride 3.4272 m per 0.6667 s cycle -> 6.435 m/s at figure scale -> 647.5 canvas px/s (1.31x the Keeper's 494)

arm_layer._from: the export's own manifest.json arm_layer block
arm_layer._rule_reversal_2026_09_29: The export's manifest says 'do NOT apply it over attack -- the slash uses the right arm and the left must swing free'. REVERSED by gandalf's design call on the scene's own measurements: without the layer the shield sits 0.249 m inside his torso during the slash (1107 of 2439 sampled vertices); with it, 54 vertices at 0.067 m. A shield-bearer holds his guard while striking with the other arm. The manifest text is left as the export wrote it; this field is what the scene obeys.
arm_layer._SUPERSEDED_2026_09_29: DO NOT USE. The export manifest's clip_selection.superseded says shield_carry_L was authored for the OLD shield placement and now puts 128 of 1829 sampled vertices inside his torso against 12 for shield_guard_L. Kept only so a scene referencing the name does not break. The armed path uses arm_layer_armed.

arm_layer_armed._over: idle, walk and run only -- it sits BELOW the block and the three one-shots in the tree, so a slash, chop, bash or block owns the left arm outright while it is running.
arm_layer_armed._source: Meshy 138 Block1, left-arm chain at 0.70 weight, already baked into the clip; the scene applies it at weight 1.0 and does not re-scale it.

_block_note: Block is a HOLD, so it is a Blend2 this script drives rather than an AnimationNodeOneShot, which cannot be held for as long as a key is down. Full body, and it roots him. WHILE BLOCKING: an input toward his strafe side side-steps at strafe_L_armed's own 93.7 px/s with his facing HELD; any other input TURNS him on the spot; he never runs. There is one strafe clip and it goes one way -- Godot has no skeleton mirroring for an AnimationTree and a mirrored body would put the shield on the wrong arm -- so right-hand input turns instead of side-stepping.
_root_motion_finding: FOUR CLIPS TRAVEL and the rest are in place -- Hips net horizontal displacement, tools/probe_root.gd: run_armed 8.6617 m (4.337 m/s), strafe_L_armed 1.8591 m (0.931 m/s), idle_armed 0.8994 m (0.184 m/s) and attack_chop 0.7519 m (0.123 m/s); walk, run, walk_armed, run_armed_locked, block and shield_bash are all under 9 mm. The first two are known; THE OTHER TWO ARE NOT FLAGGED ANYWHERE -- an idle that walks 0.90 m over its loop would have slid him sideways while standing still, and the chop lunges 0.75 m. knight.gd._deroot_all converts all four to in-place plus a speed at load, detected by measurement rather than by a list, so a re-export that fixes one cannot leave a stale entry behind.
_armed_run_choice:
SHIPPING run_armed_locked, NOT run_armed, and the export's own rule permits it -- it lists run_armed_locked as 'kept as a fallback'. MEASURED in this scene's blend space, tools/probe_transitions.gd, walk->run->walk planted-foot travel:
    run_armed         median 44.9 mm, WORST 316.2 mm  (14 planted pairs of 83)
    run_armed_locked  median 25.2 mm, worst  30.4 mm  ( 3 planted pairs of 88)
TEN TIMES BETTER on the worst frame, and the reason is structural rather than a quality difference between the clips: run_armed is a 2.5 s retargeted clip holding about FOUR gait cycles, and the sync group's whole premise is that each locomotion clip is ONE cycle. It locks walk and run to a shared cycle length lerp(walk_len, run_len, w) and aligns their contacts once; against a four-cycle clip that aligns clip-START, not foot contact, and the time scale is computed from a length that is not a period. The clip's own '0 foot slide' is true of the clip in isolation, where its root motion matches its feet -- it is not true of it driven at a speed by a blend space. To use run_armed here it needs trimming to a single gait cycle (~0.625 s) or re-exporting as a one-cycle loop; then it is strictly better, because its legs are armed motion and run_armed_locked's are the unarmed run's with only the wrists fixed.
_armed_walk_stop_unmeasurable: The armed walk stop reports 0 planted frames of 11, so there is NO number for it -- not 0 mm. walk_armed never produces a frame PAIR where the same foot is within 3 cm of its lowest on both frames with its height unchanged, at 24 fps. Reported as unmeasurable rather than as zero.
